published_statement: NOT QUOTED FROM SOURCE THIS STAGE. As transcribed by the tree's DOCKET 62 read (a1/o2.txt), not re-read: F&T Sec. 7 evaluates their static-spacetime bound (2.12) for a massless minimally coupled scalar in the Boulware (static) vacuum on the exterior Schwarzschild region r > 2M, for a static observer, using Candelas' asymptotic mode sums (7.4)/(7.5) -- the mode set split into outgoing ('up', from the past horizon) and ingoing ('in', from past null infinity) families, with greybody (horizon transmission) coefficients B_l(w) (7.6); converting to proper time via (7.7) tau_0 = |g_tt|^{1/2} t_0; the resulting bound (7.8) carries a (1-2M/r)^{-1} pole and goes arbitrarily negative at the horizon; (7.10) is the large-r/comparison form, stated to lie 'between 9/64 and 1/4' of Pfenning & Ford's Schwarzschild bound (their (tau_0/r)^2 coefficients are 16/9 of Pfenning-Ford's; (9/64)(16/9) = 1/4, checked here).
published_hypotheses: Globally static spacetime, class (2.1): ds^2 = -|g_tt| dt^2 + g_ij dx^i dx^j (READ by DOCKET 62, not re-read here)

Free real scalar, minimally coupled, here massless; normal ordering relative to the static (Boulware) vacuum -- the bound is on <:rho:>, not on rho_ren (READ by DOCKET 62; o5.txt line 3 quotes Sec. 2 verbatim)
Sampling f smooth, non-negative, O(t^-2) decay, unit integral (2.7)
Schwarzschild exterior r > 2M with M > 0, i.e. a bifurcate Killing horizon at r = 2M bounding the static region (implicit in the mode families; NAMED)

Candelas' mode basis and its asymptotic sums (7.4)/(7.5): up/in families defined by their asymptotics at the past horizon and past null infinity; B_l(w) transmission through the potential barrier from the horizon (per DOCKET 62 transcription)

Asymptotic evaluation: Candelas' sums are known in closed form only in the near-horizon and large-r limits, so (7.8)/(7.10) are limiting forms, not an exact bound at every r (per DOCKET 62 transcription; the exact status of each Sec. 7 equation is NOT re-verified here)
hypothesis_drift: NONE DROPPED by the tree's use: fewsterteo.py:56-60 keeps M > 0 and the horizon as Sec. 7's mode-defining hypothesis and refuses the M < 0 continuation; fewsterteo.py:170 SEC7_TRANSPLANTABLE_TO_NEGATIVE_M = False; fewsterteo.py:622 and ledger.py:3208-3209 check it; LEDGER.md:109 and achievable.py:264-266 repeat it.

WORDING OVER-SPECIFIC, NOT A DROPPED HYPOTHESIS -- fewsterteo.py:56-58 ('whose basis is DEFINED BY HORIZON BOUNDARY CONDITIONS ... the horizon is ... Sec. 7's mode-defining surface'): the quantity F&T's (2.12) needs, SUM_lambda |U_lambda|^2 at fixed w (and its gradient terms), is basis-INDEPENDENT -- any complete orthonormal set of positive-t-frequency modes gives the same sum, and the Boulware state itself is fixed by t-positivity, not by the up/in split. What IS horizon-defined is (i) the two-family (2-fold) structure of the continuum, which exists because r* runs over (-oo, oo) with two asymptotic ends (C1), and (ii) Candelas' asymptotic evaluation of the sums and the B_l(w). At M < 0 the r* domain has one asymptotic end (C2) and the continuum is at most 1-fold per (l,m), so there is no up/in pair to continue -- the tree's conclusion is right; its phrasing puts the dependence on 'the basis' where it sits on the domain's two-endedness and on Candelas' asymptotics.

HYPOTHESIS THE TREE DOES NOT NAME (an ADDITION a would-be M < 0 analogue would need, strengthening the refusal): at M < 0 the radial operator is LIMIT CIRCLE at the naked singularity r = 0 (x^2 V -> -1/4 for every l; both sqrt(x) and sqrt(x) ln x are L^2), so it is not essentially self-adjoint and even the static 'vacuum' needs a chosen boundary condition at r = 0 (a one-parameter family per l). fewsterteo.py:56-60 names 'no horizon' but not this; it is a second, independent reason Sec. 7 has no M < 0 counterpart. Machine-checked here (C3), not read at source.

fewsterteo.py:59 'the horizon is not a caveat on Sec. 7' vs the DOCKET 62 O2 row's earlier 'the horizon caveat PROVABLY CANNOT BITE' (a1/o2.txt): the tree already records the correction -- the (1-2M/r)^{-1} pole of (7.8) cannot bite at M < 0 (C2: F > 0 on r > 0), but that is not a licence to continue (7.10). lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. Sec. 7 is not an extrapolation from data: it is a mode-sum evaluation in closed/asymptotic form with M a free parameter, and the only 'datum' the tree's use turns on is the sign of M, which is the corridor's design (M < 0), not a measurement. What F&T (1998) and Candelas (1980) 'lacked' is not data but a construction they never attempted: an M < 0 mode basis. Evidence AGAINST M's suspicion biting here: nothing measured since 1998 bears on Sec. 7, and no datum moves it (data_at_publication: none). Evidence that the gap is REAL but is a gap in scope, not an error: at M < 0 there is no horizon (C2), the r* domain is one-ended so the up/in two-family structure does not exist (C1 vs C2), and the radial operator is limit circle at r = 0 so the static state needs an extra boundary-condition choice (C3). Having a 'missing' M < 0 computation would therefore not correct Sec. 7; it would be a different theorem resting on an added hypothesis (the r = 0 boundary condition) that the tree does not presently name. Conclusion unchanged: Sec. 7 as used (M > 0 only, refused at M < 0) is not undermined by anything F&T lacked.
